children: A Dataset is a named content space — production is the canonical one — and the unit the Indx Engine rebuilds blue/green into versioned shadow copies.

A Dataset groups Documents into a content space addressable by name. In Barkpark the live space is production. Datasets sit inside the Workspace + Project tenancy hierarchy, so two tenants can each hold their own production Dataset without collision.

When the Indx Engine (the Indx Retriever Seam) indexes a Dataset, it does not mutate in place. It rebuilds into a versioned shadow named bp_<scope>_vN — for example bp_production_v7 — then atomically flips reads to the new version. This Blue Green Rebuild is what lets the Edge Projector and Search indexes regenerate without ever serving a half-built corpus. The vN suffix is the version that just went live; the previous one lingers as the instant rollback target.

A Dataset is the scope you name when reading content over the HTTP API v1 — e.g. /v1/data/query/production/post — one of the routes catalogued under API and Contracts. The active Perspective (published vs drafts) layers on top of the Dataset to decide which Document rows are visible, and the Content Graph corpus draws its nodes from the published view of the Dataset. As a named content space, the Dataset is the addressable layer of the Content Model beneath the Workspace + Project tenancy key.

Dataset rebuilds are driven by Oban Workers on the Phoenix API, triggered by mutations and surfaced through Webhooks / Cache Revalidation. The set of queryable Datasets is announced through the Capabilities Manifest so the bp CLI can target the right one.
